channel.title: Today's Walk, Let's Talk
channel.description: Today's Walk, Let's Talk is a short audio show about dogs: why they sniff, how they bond with people, and what recent research can and cannot say. Every voice is an AI character, not a real person and not a veterinarian, trainer or researcher. Episodes share general information only. Where an episode draws on a published study, the links appear on the episode page so you can read the source yourself. For your dog's health or behavior, ask your own vet or a qualified trainer. Cover art and character portraits are AI-generated and do not depict real people. The show is made by TurtleRock Paws, a dog boarding business in Irvine, California.

item.title: Journal Club: how selective breeding reshaped the dog brain
item.description: A peer-reviewed brain-imaging study looked at scans from 62 healthy pet dogs across 33 breeds and found that the shape of the dog brain varies in real, patterned ways from one lineage to another. The variation lines up with the jobs dogs were bred for, and most of it sits on the newest branches of the dog family tree, the fast, recent remaking of breeds that took off in the Victorian era. AI voices sharing general information, not veterinary advice. For your dog's health, ask your vet.

item.title: Journal Club: the teenage dog phase
item.description: A peer-reviewed study followed young dogs being raised as future guide dogs and found that, around eight months old, the odds of a dog repeatedly not answering a well-known cue from the person who raised them were higher, but not with someone else, and that carers rated their dogs as easier to train again by about a year. Our readers read the whole article: what it found, why it is only part of the story, and three calm take-homes. AI voices sharing general information, not veterinary advice. For your dog's health, ask your vet.
